newsitem.title: USA: Consumer prices rise 0.1 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: Consumer prices rise 0.1 percent in March.

text.p: Consumer prices moved up modestly in March, the Labor Department said Tuesday, new evidence of still largely quiet inflation despite growing concern that price pressures may be building.
The department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent in the month after being up 0.3 percent in February.

With the often volatile food and energy sector left out, the so-called core rate that economists believe more closely follows underlying inflation trends, rose 0.2 percent after being up the same amount in February.
The March data was better than Wall Street estimates that the overall index would rise 0.2 percent and the underlying or core rate would increase 0.3 percent.
The department said energy prices fell 1.7 percent after rising 0.3 percent in February, while food prices were unchanged after being up 0.3 percent in February. Gasoline was off 2.1 percent.
The new data on inflation comes after last week's report showing that while wholesale prices notched lower in March, they moved disturbingly higher at the underlying level.

The Federal Reserve has been on the hunt for inflation pressures since raising rates to counter head them off last month and many analysts believe they will raise them again when policymakers gather on May 20.
One big culprit in the rise in underlying consumer prices was airline fares, which rose 4.5 percent in part because of the reimposition of the 10 percent airline fare tax.
Apparel costs, which rose 0.2 percent in February, fell 0.3 percent.
The department said transportation costs edged up 0.1 percent after falling 0.1 percent in February, while entertainment matched the 0.2 percent rise in February.
Housing prices were unchanged after risng 0.3 percent in February.
